name: fibroblast growth factor receptor 2
pathways: negative regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II
positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

function.text: FGFR2 encodes fibroblast growth factor receptor 2. Annotated molecular activities include protein tyrosine kinase activity and protein homodimerization activity. It participates in negative regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II and positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to Apert syndrome (autosomal dominant); Beare-Stevenson cutis gyrata syndrome (autosomal dominant). Additional curated associations are listed below.

somatic.text: Reported somatic alteration contexts include Gastric adenocarcinoma; Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma; Small-duct intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. The alteration class and exact variant must be assessed in the disease context.

function.text: FGFR2 encodes fibroblast growth factor receptor 2. It is a tyrosine-protein kinase that acts as a cell-surface receptor for fibroblast growth factors and plays an essential role in the regulation of cell proliferation, differentiation, migration and apoptosis, and in the regulation of embryonic development. It is required for normal embryonic patterning, trophoblast function, limb bud development, lung morphogenesis, osteogenesis and skin development. It contributes to the regulation of osteoblast differentiation, proliferation and apoptosis, and is required for normal skeleton development.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Apert syndrome (autosomal dominant); Beare-Stevenson cutis gyrata syndrome (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving FGFR2 have been reported in gastric adenocarcinoma, intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, and small-duct intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
